Model evaluation

Each sampled task was asked twice: with its image, and without it. Reference answers come from the scene data, never from a model, so a wrong model answer is the model's mistake unless the human audit finds otherwise. Contrast pairs ask the same question about a minimally edited image with a different answer; a model that reads the image gets both right. Sample: 150 of 150 tasks, spread across templates.

Contrast pairs

129 of 150 tasks have a twin: the same question about an image where one value was edited so the answer changes, with the axis pinned so nothing else moves. The median edit moves one value by 12% of the value axis. Both images pass the same gates. A model that answers from the question text alone can't get both right.

OCR read-back

An independent check of the grounding gate, which trusts the renderer's layout record. Every label a question depends on was cropped out of the final PNG and read by tesseract 5.5.3, an OCR engine unrelated to the models being evaluated. A label counts as read back when the OCR text matches what was drawn (characters OCR commonly confuses, such as O and 0, count as equal). The crops below show what OCR saw.
